title: Quoin Retail - latency echo fix validation & risk acceptance
summary: Quick validation of the latency-echo hotfix that was rolled yesterday, discussion of residual risk, acceptance criteria for SLA remediation, and agreement on a short pilot and rollback window.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (Quoin VP Eng), Priya Shah (Quoin SRE), Liam O'Connor (Quoin CTO)
Recording note: partial captions, occasional mis-words (K V cache, Redwood Optimise)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, uh, quick agenda — sanity-check the hotfix we pushed last night, go over telemetry, confirm acceptance criteria for the SLA remediation and align on the pilot window. Jordan, do you want to kick off with what you saw this morning?

[00:18] Jordan: Yeah, thanks. So, um, first off thanks for the quick patch, we saw a drop in the 95th percentile within our staging cluster. There still are a few spikes around midday load tests, like 740 to 1,200 ms for a small subset. But overall it's a big improvement.

[00:41] Priya: To add — we ran a full synthetic suite at 08:00 and 12:00, traffic shape matched prod closely, prefix cache hit moved from 62% to about 78%, which aligns with the patch that changed prefix caching TTLs. However, we noticed some long tails when we hammer with large batch transforms, there might be a batching interaction.

[01:05] Ethan: Right, that matches our expectation. The regression was due to a routing fallback loop where requests were being routed to a cold path repeatedly because the K V cache invalidation was too aggressive. The hotfix narrows the invalidation window and adds a short de-dupe on the router. We saw improved steady-state latencies in our internal bench.

[01:32] Liam: Quick clarification — when you say K V cache invalidation, is that on the client side or on the serving nodes? We thought it was the client TTL in our SDK.

[01:44] Ethan: It's server-side. The node-level KV store that tracks model shards was expiring entries under heavy eviction pressure; the router then treated capacity as unavailable and triggered fallback to a heavier variant repeatedly. So it was a server routing symptom, not the SDK TTL.

[02:12] Jordan: Ok that helps. We did see multiple fallback-to-variant events in the logs. The only odd bit: some of the fallback events correlate with regional failover that happened during our load test. Could be amplification.

[02:31] Maya: Amplification is the right word. That's why the hotfix included a short cooldown and a backoff multiplier to avoid repeated flip-flopping.

[02:42] Priya: We also want to call out the noise in token counts — the sampling in our metric pipeline mis-attributes longer sequences to the wrong route sometimes and it makes the cost numbers jittery. Noting that since we need to sign off on cost impact for the acceptance.

[03:05] Ethan: We can supply a corrected metric export. There was an ingestion parser edge case where the route label was trunc'd. Expect a fixed CSV link after this call.

[03:18] Maya: Cool. Can you walk us through the validation numbers you ran, Ethan?

[03:24] Ethan: Sure — internal bench compared pre-hotfix vs post-hotfix: 95p dropped 320ms -> 90ms on 8k token synthetic, 99p dropped 1.1s -> 420ms. CPU steal on the GPU boxes was reduced when we pinned kernels, and batch variance is lower. In staging with Quoin's traffic replay, P95 reduced by ~55%. There are residual 99.9 spikes under pathological batching coordination; we're still targeting those.

[04:03] Jordan: OK good. What are the known residual risks? We need to present them to compliance and product.

[04:10] Ethan: Residual risk list: 1) long-tail spikes with adversarial batch shapes, 2) regional failover amplification during high GC cycles, 3) rare KV cache thrash when we hit a corner-case with model swapping. Those are mitigations we have planned but not yet validated at scale.

[04:37] Priya: For #1, can you quantify what 'adversarial' means? Is this something our client calls could create?

[04:44] Ethan: It would be a very specific pattern — very small requests interleaved with very large streamed requests that cause packing to create tiny batches followed by a big one. It's unlikely in your normal user workload but possible in batch export jobs.

[05:03] Liam: That's something we can guard on our side by limiting client-side batch sizes in the next SDK rev. But for the short-term we need to accept some residual risk if numbers are within agreed delta.

[05:17] Maya: Let's talk acceptance criteria then. Jordan, Priya — what's your bar? Typically customers ask for P95 <= 200ms over baseline and P99 <= 800ms; is that reasonable here?

[05:31] Jordan: Historically Quoin baseline is P95 180ms, P99 650ms. Post-hotfix we're seeing P95 ~210-230ms in a few windows. If you can guarantee a pilot window where we can run production traffic at 10% and not see regressions for 72 hours, leadership might accept a risk exception for full SLA.

[05:54] Priya: Also need audit logs showing routing decisions (for SOC2 questions) and KMS key usage. We had a security review last week and they flagged that as required.

[06:07] Maya: We'll provide the routing trace logs — redwood produces per-request traces, will redact PII and provide the trace bundle. KMS logs are separate — we can share the integration notes and the hashed request IDs.

[06:23] Ethan: I'll attach a short runbook for the rollback plan. It includes a canary rollback that's immediate and a staged rollback over 30 minutes if we see elevated error rates.

[06:39] Jordan: What's the rollback risk? If we rollback, will we reintroduce the original routing loop?

[06:45] Ethan: Rolling back restores previous behavior including the aggressive invalidation, so we wouldn't re-trigger the loop immediately if we rollback carefully — but yes, under load it could reappear. That's why the canary and the monitoring thresholds are critical.

[07:02] Priya: Can we get the exact monitoring queries and alert thresholds? We'll plug them into our pagerduty.

[07:08] Maya: Yes — we'll push the PromQL snippets and SLO thresholds after the call.

[07:15] Liam: And timeline — when can you share the corrected metrics CSV and the runbook?

[07:20] Ethan: I'll upload corrected metrics and the runbook by EOD tomorrow, Nov 20.

[07:27] Maya: For the pilot, we're proposing: start Monday Nov 24 at 00:00 UTC, run a 72-hour 10% traffic pilot with rollback windows at 18 and 36 hours. Does that work?

[07:39] Jordan: Monday is fine. We'll need to update stakeholders and make sure our risk board signs off.

[07:45] Priya: Also want a short dry-run of the rollback on Friday dev environment so ops knows the steps.

[07:51] Ethan: We can schedule a 30-minute drill Friday at 16:00 UTC — simulate canary fail and execute rollback.

[07:59] Maya: Great. A few housekeeping items: we'll send a short patch note doc, a sensitive runbook link, and the metric exports. Can we also get a brief cost delta estimate for the pilot? Priya — do you want token/cost gating?

[08:12] Priya: Yes — show cost delta for the worst 3 hours during the pilot and expected monthly delta if we keep the config. That informs procurement.

[08:21] Ethan: We ran a rough cost model — worst-case extra 8% token compute cost under high retry load, best case <1%. We will provide more precise numbers with corrected metrics.

[08:35] Jordan: One more security question: how long will routing traces be retained on your side? Our compliance team wants 90 days.

[08:42] Maya: Default is 30 days for hosted, but we can extend to 90 days for enterprise accounts; that will be part of the support commitment for your Dedicated tier. We'll include options.

[08:55] Liam: Alright let's recap action items and owners.

[09:01] Maya: Yes — recap then close.

[09:05] (Crosstalk)

[09:10] End of transcript notes: minor word swaps (Redwood Optimise -> Redwood Optimize), occasional truncation in metric labels, timestamps are approximate.
next_steps: Redwood to upload corrected metric CSV and rollback runbook by 2025-11-20 (Ethan)
Schedule rollback dry-run in Quoin dev on 2025-11-21 16:00 UTC (Ethan + Priya)
Start 72-hour 10% pilot on 2025-11-24 00:00 UTC (Jordan to confirm)
Provide audit log retention options and pricing by 2025-11-21 (Maya)
Send cost delta analysis for pilot by 2025-11-20 (Ethan)

Ethan Cho + Priya Shah - run rollback dry-run in dev - due: 2025-11-21
